text: 你打听哈里斯教授的遗孀阿米莉娅的情况。桑福德先生很乐意告诉你这些闲话。
“阿米莉娅·哈里斯。几年前她和哈里斯教授搬到这里。挺年轻漂亮的女人。她丈夫死后，她看起来还撑得住。我跟你说，她挺有胆量。她像是出身老钱人家的人，跟大多数埃斯伯里的新来者一样。不过她今晚在拍卖丈夫留下的一些东西，所以我猜她是缺钱了。别的我就说不上来了。我不太了解她。”桑福德耸耸肩，笑了笑。
你又和桑福德寒暄了几句，他便去完成引船进港的工作。你和其他乘客闲聊，看看周围景色，以此打发时间。你注意到埃斯伯里湖岸边高耸的松树和起伏的山丘。这些景色以及远处的小镇，都隐约可见于逐渐浓密的雾气之中；你眯起眼睛，终于看得清楚些。
最后，你们抵达埃斯伯里的码头，你很庆幸终于离开了水面。

en.title: Alone Against the Tide · 89
text: You ask after Prof. Harris’ widow, Amelia. Mr. Sanford is only too happy to give you the gossip.

“Amelia Harris. She moved here with Professor Harris a few years back. Pretty young broad. Seems to be holding it together after her husband’s death, though. She’s got some pluck, I’ll tell ya that. She seems like the type who comes from old money, just like most of the newcomers to Esbury. But she’s selling off some of her late husband’s things tonight, so I guess she needs the dough. I can’t say much beyond that. I don’t know her all that well.” Sanford shrugs and smiles.

You exchange a few more pleasantries with Sanford before he goes off to finish guiding the boat into port. You pass the time in casual conversation with the other passengers and in observing the scenery. You note the tall pines and the sloping hills along the lakeshore around Esbury. These features, and the small town beyond, are just visible through the growing mist, but squinting helps make them out to your satisfaction.
In time, you arrive on the pier at Esbury, grateful to be off the water.
